source_evidence.english_after: When executing a VTBS 20R RNP approach, note the following: After the ATKIN, the control may instruct to "maintain 5000ft, turn right HDG 165, intercept final course 20R, report established." Note that the control requires establishing the 20R RNP five sides first, not granting permission for the RNP approach. Pay attention tothe confirmation instructions toavoid mistakenly awaiting the APPR. Subsequently, the control may descend 3500ft, allowing the RNP 20R approach, which could cause excessive energy. The crew should prepare contingency plans to prevent instability. The "high intercept" procedure is not permitted during RNP approaches.

Note that the control requires establishing the 20R RNP five sides first, not granting permission for the RNP approach. Pay attention tothe confirmation instructions toavoid mistakenly awaiting the APPR. Subsequently, the control may descend 3500ft, allowing the RNP 20R approach, which could cause excessive energy. The crew should prepare contingency plans to prevent instability. The "high intercept" procedure is not permitted during RNP approaches.

other_phase_english_candidates.text: When executing a VTBS 20R RNP approach, note the following: After the ATKIN, the control may instruct to "maintain 5000ft, turn right HDG 165, intercept final course 20R, report established." Note that the control requires establishing the 20R RNP five sides first, not granting permission for the RNP approach. Pay attention tothe confirmation instructions toavoid mistakenly awaiting the APPR. Subsequently, the control may descend 3500ft, allowing the RNP 20R approach, which could cause excessive energy. The crew should prepare contingency plans to prevent instability. The "high intercept" procedure is not permitted during RNP approaches.

other_phase_english_candidates.text: When executing a VTBS 20R RNP approach, note the following: After the ATKIN, the control may instruct to "maintain 5000ft, turn right HDG 165, intercept final course 20R, report established." Note that the control requires establishing the 20R RNP five sides first, not granting permission for the RNP approach. Pay attention tothe confirmation instructions toavoid mistakenly awaiting the APPR. Subsequently, the control may descend 3500ft, allowing the RNP 20R approach, which could cause excessive energy. The crew should prepare contingency plans to prevent instability. The "high intercept" procedure is not permitted during RNP approaches.
